title: Graceful SLO breach mitigator and pulsebacker hotfix
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes premature circuit re-open in pulsebacker SLO mitigator; adds safer fallback traffic shaping and additional telemetry for SLO breach windows.
description: Motivation: a recent incident (SUP-4421) exposed oscillations when regional slowpaths briefly breached tenant SLOs: circuits reopened on a single successful probe and traffic immediately shifted back causing a cycle of open/close with increased tail latency. This PR implements a two-part hotfix: 1) introduce a reopen_debounce window and persistent reopen backoff for the pulsebacker SLO mitigator so a single probe cannot re-open a circuit; 2) add a graceful diversion mode ("pulseback") that slowly reintroduces traffic to healthier replicas with controlled pacing and transient token-throttling instead of an all-or-nothing failover. Goals: stop oscillations, reduce tail latency amplification during recovery, and provide observability for future tuning. Changes include runtime logic and conservative default config so behavior is opt-in-per-tenant until a follow-up rollout. Checklist: - implement reopen_debounce and reopen_backoff counters in slo_mitigator runtime; - add pulseback diversion algorithm and token-shaper with configurable ramp-rate; - fix circuit state persistence bug where transient probe success cleared sticky_reopen flag; - add telemetry (slo_mitigator.latency_window, pulsebacker.divert_rate, pulsebacker.reopen_debounce_count) and dashboard snippets; - integration tests simulating steady-state and noisy probe flapping; - add runbook note under docs/operational for on-call steps and rollback. Testing: unit tests added for state machine paths; integration simulation that runs a 60s noisy-probe scenario shows circuits stay closed for configured debounce window and diversion ramps from 5% -> 50% over 30s without oscillation. CI history: initial CI run flagged a flaky probe unit test (probe_fuzzy_backoff_test) due to a timing assumption; updated test to use a deterministic clock and re-ran — CI passed. Rollout plan: merge hotfix to main, enable feature-flag to a small cohort of tenants for 48h, monitor new metrics and slowpath latencies, then widen. Rollback: revert feature-flag and configuration; state persistence changes include a migration-safe toggle. Risks: misconfigured ramp rates could increase median latency slightly during recovery; conservative defaults chosen to avoid impact. Related: ENG-2198 tracks the production rollout and param tuning; ENG-2320 is a follow-up to expose tenant-level control in Console. This is a non-breaking runtime patch but touches circuit persistence and routing; coordinated rollouts with SRE required.

notes_for_oncall: If tenants report oscillation after rollout: enable emergency feature-flag off, inspect pulsebacker.divert_rate and slo_mitigator.reopen_debounce_count; if circuits remain sticky open for >5m, trigger circuit_store rollback.
changelog_summary: Hotfix: safer reopen debounce and staged traffic reintroduction (pulseback) to prevent oscillatory reopen/close cycles during transient SLO breaches.
security_considerations: No user data changes; metrics use cohort tagging; no new network endpoints exposed.
follow_up_actions: 1) Dashboard tuning and alert on pulsebacker.divert_rate > 60% for any cohort; 2) Console control to surface tenant-level ramp-rate (ENG-2320); 3) Canary rollout to 10% of tenants for 72h and collect telemetry (ENG-2198).
